source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
finding: One model writes, critiques and rewrites its own output. Across 7 tasks with GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, outputs improved by about 20% absolute on average over one-step generation. This is the closest machine copy of 'the situation talks back, the designer revises'.
numbers: 7 tasks; GPT-4 code optimization 27.3% to 36.0% (+8.7 abs); GPT-4 dialogue preference 25.4% to 74.6% (+49.2).
quote: improving by 20% absolute on average in task performance
limits: Gains are largest on open-ended, taste-based tasks (dialogue, sentiment, acronyms), judged partly by GPT-4 as proxy (82%/68%/71% agreement with humans). Weak on math.
agent_relevance: Supports a revise loop (S5/O8) for open-ended output, but the largest gains come where there is no checkable ground truth, which is where G3 warns about fitting.

source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine, math reasoning result
finding: On math, self-feedback barely helped because the model could not see its own error. A reasoning chain that looks consistent fools the critic.
numbers: ChatGPT feedback said 'everything looks good' for 94% of instances; gains became 5%+ larger when an external source said the answer was wrong (Appendix H.1).
limits: ChatGPT specific; external signal helped.
agent_relevance: Matches G2: revise only from real failing output, not from the model's own opinion that something is wrong.

source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine, feedback ablation
finding: Quality of the 'back-talk' matters. Specific, actionable feedback beat generic feedback, which beat no feedback.
numbers: Sentiment reversal: 43.2 specific vs 31.2 generic vs 0 none. Acronym: 56.4 vs 54.0 vs 48.0. Code optimization: 27.5 vs 26.0 vs 24.8.
limits: Small differences on code; measured on tasks with metrics the authors designed.
agent_relevance: When the agent reflects, the prompt should force the critique to name a concrete place and a concrete action, as the schema's G2 already requires.

source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine, iteration curve
finding: More feedback-refine rounds help with diminishing returns. Quality can move up on one aspect and down on another between rounds.
numbers: Code optimization 22.0 to 28.8 over 3 rounds; sentiment 33.9 to 36.8; constrained generation 29.0 to 49.7.
limits: Not monotone on multi-aspect tasks such as acronyms; they select the best-scoring round.
agent_relevance: Cap revise rounds (about 2-3) and keep the best version by a code-computed score, not the last one.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet (ICLR 2024)
finding: Reported self-correction gains came from using ground-truth labels to decide when to stop. With oracle labels, accuracy rose. With no oracle (intrinsic self-correction), accuracy fell.
numbers: GPT-3.5 standard 75.9 GSM8K / 75.8 CommonSenseQA / 26.0 HotpotQA; with oracle 84.3 / 89.7 / 29.0; intrinsic round 2 on GSM8K 74.7 and CommonSenseQA 41.8.
quote: the improvements vanish when oracle labels are not available
limits: GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4-Turbo, Llama-2; 3 benchmarks; some critics say prompts were not the best ones.
agent_relevance: Direct support for G1 and G2. Reflection without an external signal is not safe.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet, GPT-4 table
finding: Even GPT-4 got slightly worse after intrinsic self-correction on GSM8K and HotpotQA. The stronger model changed its answer less often.
numbers: GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 (round 1) to 89.0 (round 2); CommonSenseQA 82.0 to 79.5 to 80.0; HotpotQA 49.0 to 49.0 to 43.0. With oracle GPT-4 reached 97.5 / 85.5 / 59.0.
limits: Sample sizes not checked in this pass; differences of 1-3 points may be within noise.
agent_relevance: A 'reflect once more' step costs calls and can lower accuracy. Gate it on a signal.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet, why it fails
finding: Models flip correct answers to wrong ones more often than the reverse. The model cannot judge its own reasoning. Different feedback prompts did not rescue it. A model told 'review and find problems' tends to invent problems.
numbers: GSM8K GPT-3.5 kept its first answer 74.7% of the time over two rounds; Llama-2 GSM8K 62.0 to 43.5 to 36.5. Three different feedback prompts on GPT-4-Turbo gave 88.0-91.0 vs 91.5 baseline on GSM8K.
limits: Prompt wording that primes doubt ('assume it could be wrong') is an artifact of prompt framing.
agent_relevance: Forced doubt hurts. Our own word-puzzle result (92% plain vs 75% forced doubt) fits this.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet, constrained generation and fair-compute note
finding: Some earlier gains came from a better initial prompt or from spending more calls, not from reflection. Self-consistency with the same number of calls matched or beat multi-agent debate.
numbers: Self-consistency 9 responses reached about 88.2 on GSM8K vs debate lower in Table 7 (exact pairing of rows not verified in layout).
limits: Table layout garbled by text extraction, so debate-vs-SC pairing not certain.
agent_relevance: Compare reflection against the same compute spent on plain resampling (G4).

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: After a failed trial the agent writes a first-person verbal reflection, stores it in memory, and tries again. Success rose on coding, reasoning and game tasks.
numbers: HumanEval pass@1 91% vs GPT-4 80%; AlfWorld +22% absolute over baselines in 12 iterative trials; HotPotQA +20%; ReAct-only AlfWorld agent plateaued at 22% hallucination rate.
quote: surpassing the previous state-of-the-art GPT-4 that achieves 80%
limits: Needs a binary success signal from the environment or unit tests. Authors name local minima and test-writing limits. Huang et al. note the oracle dependence.
agent_relevance: Best match to O8: reflect after a real failed check, store the lesson. The trigger is an external signal, which fits G1.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion, ablations
finding: On HotPotQA with given context, adding a written self-reflection step beat just keeping the last trajectory in memory. This separates 'reflecting' from 'merely retrying with history'.
numbers: Self-reflection gave an 8% absolute boost over the episodic-memory-only variant (100 HotPotQA questions).
limits: Single ablation on 100 questions; no confidence intervals in the main text.
agent_relevance: Writing the lesson in words seems to add value over raw history. Worth testing in S5.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion, code evaluation
finding: Self-written unit tests are the 'back-talk' signal in code. Test quality limits reflection quality: false positives let wrong code pass.
numbers: Test-generation precision on MBPP Python: false positive rate 16.3% vs 1.4% on HumanEval Python; reported 82% and 80% on related rates.
limits: Test-driven setup fits code, not open design problems.
agent_relevance: G3: a self-made test is weaker proof than a held-out test; Reflexion's MBPP weakness is an example.

source: Kamoi et al. (2024) When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey
finding: Survey of self-correction research. No prior work shows success with feedback from a prompted LLM alone, except in tasks that are unusually suited to it. Self-correction works when reliable external feedback exists. Large-scale fine-tuning also enables it. The bottleneck is generating good feedback.
numbers: Three headline conclusions; papers up to May 2024; checklist for fair experiments.
quote: no prior work demonstrates successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs
limits: Survey; judgments about which studies are fair are the authors' own.
agent_relevance: The decisive rule for O8: supply feedback from code, tests, tools or held-out data. Do not rely on prompted self-critique.

source: Gou et al. (2024) CRITIC: LLMs Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing (ICLR 2024)
finding: Critique through tools (search, code interpreter, toxicity API) improves outputs. Removing the tool and letting the model critique itself removed most of the gain, sometimes made it worse.
numbers: Text-Davinci-003 math program synthesis: GSM8k PoT 70.1 to CRITIC 72.2 (+2.1) vs CRITIC without tool 68.3 (-1.8); TabMWP 64.6 to 87.6 with tool vs 84.9 without; SVAMP 84.0 to 80.7 both ways.
limits: Gains differ by dataset and model; SVAMP fell. Free-form QA results not mapped to model in this note.
agent_relevance: Tool feedback is the real conversation with the situation; the model's own opinion is not.

source: Gou et al. (2024) CRITIC, QA ablation
finding: In open-domain QA, the variant without search evidence scored below plain chain-of-thought in one reported block, while the full tool version scored above it.
numbers: One QA table block: CoT 44.2, CRITIC w/o Tool 42.0, CRITIC 50.0 (metric and model not pinned down from the layout).
limits: Table layout garbled; treat the numbers as indicative only.
agent_relevance: Same message as c13: reflection without an external check can be net negative.

source: Tyen et al. (2024) LLMs cannot find reasoning errors, but can correct them given the error location
finding: Splits self-correction into finding the mistake and fixing it. Finding is the weak part. Correction is strong once the location is given. Location from a small trained classifier worked without in-domain labels.
numbers: BIG-Bench Mistake: 2186 chain-of-thought traces, 5 tasks; GPT-4 best at 52.87 overall mistake-finding accuracy by step prompting.
limits: Traces from PaLM 2; tasks are objective with a single clear mistake.
agent_relevance: Have code locate the failing step; let the model only repair it. Fits G2 exactly.

source: Tyen et al. (2024) backtracking experiment
finding: Backtracking with the true mistake location raised accuracy on wrong traces much more than a random location. Both cost some accuracy on traces that were already right.
numbers: Gain on originally wrong traces with true location: +18.04 to +43.92 (5 tasks); random location: +5.16 to +21.57. Loss on originally right traces: 0.00 to -11.43 (true) and -6.67 to -15.91 (random).
limits: Task order in extracted table uncertain; ranges are safe, task pairing is not.
agent_relevance: Reflecting on a correct answer is costly; only reflect when the failure is flagged.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Teaching Large Language Models to Self-Debug (ICLR 2024)
finding: The model explains its code line by line (rubber duck style) and uses execution results to fix it. Largest effect when unit tests give real feedback.
numbers: Spider: +2-3% baseline, +9% on hardest queries; TransCoder and MBPP with unit tests: up to +12%; matched or beat baselines drawing over 10x more candidates.
limits: Code-only; the gain with explanation but no tests is small.
agent_relevance: A concrete agent-loop form of reflection-in-action: run, see output, explain, patch. Sample-efficient compared to resampling.

source: Kumar et al. (2024) Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning (SCoRe)
finding: Prompted self-correction on MATH made the base Gemini model worse. Prompting methods and plain SFT gave little. Multi-turn RL on own data gave a positive correction gain.
numbers: MATH: base accuracy 52.6% to 41.4% after revision (-11.2); Self-Refine -1.0; STaR +0.4; Pair-SFT +1.8; SCoRe 60.0% to 64.4% (+4.4). HumanEval: SCoRe +12.2 (52.4% to 64.6%) vs base +3.0, Self-Refine -1.2.
limits: Needs training; Gemini 1.0 Pro / 1.5 Flash only; we cannot train.
agent_relevance: Shows the capability is trainable but absent by default. For a scaffold-only agent, assume no free self-correction.

source: Tsui (2026) Self-Correction Bench (COLM 2026)
finding: The same error is fixed when attributed to the user but left alone when attributed to the model itself. This is a blind spot in activation, not in knowledge.
numbers: 14 open-source non-reasoning models; average blind spot 64.5%.
quote: models correct external errors but fail on identical internal ones
limits: Open non-reasoning models only; injected error setup.
agent_relevance: Strong reason to show the model its own earlier output as if it came from someone else (a 'reviewer view') when revising.

source: Tsui (2026) Self-Correction Bench, the 'Wait' fix
finding: Appending 'Wait' after the model's own erroneous output restores correction with no training. Other markers like 'But' and 'However' work less well. Fine-tuning on a few correction traces also shrinks the blind spot.
numbers: 'Wait' cut the blind spot by 89.3% on average and raised mean accuracy by 156%; 5,306 correction traces cut it by 76.0%.
limits: Gain is relative to the blind-spot gap, not absolute accuracy; 'Wait' also can cause doubt on correct answers (not measured in what I read).
agent_relevance: A cheap O8 trigger phrase, but under G1 it should fire only on a signal.

source: Sinlapanuntakul et al. (2026) How Designers Envision Value-Oriented AI Design Concepts with Generative AI (DIS 2026)
finding: 18 designers used ChatGPT to develop AI concepts. The authors describe 'reciprocal reflection-in-action': the material (AI) interprets intent and answers back, unlike clay or paper. Three modes: value externalization, interpretive encounter, reflective redirection.
numbers: 18 designers; 16 of 18 struggled to turn abstract values into concrete, communicable ideas.
limits: Qualitative, small N, one tool; no outcome measure of design quality.
agent_relevance: Writing a prompt forced designers to sharpen their own intent. For our agent, the restate step may act the same way.

source: Ahn et al. (2026) From Answer Givers to Design Mentors (DesignMentor)
finding: An LLM that asks questions (cognitive apprenticeship: articulate, coach, scaffold) was compared with a plain answer-giving LLM for visualization design. It scored higher on complete feedback loops, metacognitive awareness and relevance, but took more effort.
numbers: Within-subjects study, 25 participants in the main evaluation (24 in formative work); 16 questionnaire items on 5-point scale; effectiveness varied by design phase.
limits: Self-report; small sample; domain is data visualization.
agent_relevance: Question-first reflection beats answer-giving for a human designer; the agent equivalent is to question its own plan against the output.

source: Kimm and Tan (2025) ChatGraPhT: Visual Conversation Interface for Multi-Path Reflection
finding: Tool that shows chat as a branchable map, with two agentic LLM assistants giving moment-to-moment (reflection-in-action) and higher-level (reflection-on-action) guidance. Authors claim a linear chat transcript limits reflection.
numbers: No sample: exploratory first-person enquiry; the paper says it is not an evaluative study.
limits: No measured effect.
agent_relevance: Idea for multi-path revision: keep abandoned branches visible so revision does not erase them.

source: Material for Thought: Generative AI as an Active Creative Medium (2026)
finding: Conceptual paper: generative AI is a medium that actively drifts toward resolution, so the human role shifts from evaluator to orchestrator. Proposes Shape, Observe, Stir, Select.
numbers: No data; framework only.
limits: Untested theory.
agent_relevance: Warns that an LLM's own drift toward closure may cut short the exploration that back-talk is supposed to give; premature closure should be code-checked.

source: Sinlapanuntakul et al. (2026) DIS 2026, boundary on Schön's assumption
finding: The authors note Schön's account assumes materials that respond predictably and transparently. An LLM material interprets and can mislead, so the conversation has two interpreting sides.
numbers: Qualitative; 18 designers.
limits: Interpretation by the authors from interviews and think-aloud.
agent_relevance: For an LLM agent, the 'situation' we want it to listen to should be code output, not another LLM's opinion.

source: Kokotovich (2015) critique of reflection-in-action, as cited in the task brief
finding: Argued the account leans on tacit experience and narrows what a designer considers. Not opened this session.
limits: Secondhand from the task text.
agent_relevance: Machine analogue: reflection built only on the model's own prior text narrows search; this matches the correlated-error warning (G4).

source: Synthesis across c01-c20
finding: Pattern across 2023-2026 machine studies: reflection helps when the 'back-talk' is outside the model (tests, tools, oracle, true error location) and when it is specific. Prompted self-critique alone is flat or negative on reasoning tasks, and positive mainly on open-ended taste tasks.
numbers: Positive: Reflexion +22 ALFWorld, Self-Debug up to +12, CRITIC tool-based. Negative: Huang GSM8K 75.9 to 74.7, CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 41.8, Gemini MATH -11.2.
limits: Mixed models and metrics; most tests are on GPT-3.5/4 era models. Newer reasoning models only touched by c19.
agent_relevance: Keep S5 revise gated by code-found failures; show the model its own output as external text; cap rounds; keep best version.

source: Search gap note
finding: I found no LLM study that directly tests Schön's reflection-in-action as a hypothesis against human designers with matched tasks. OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar APIs were rate limited this session and the WebSearch budget ran out after one query, so older computational design systems (for example from Gero's group) were not checked.
limits: Gap in coverage; a second pass should look for design-agent papers (sketch-and-critique with vision models) and older AI design systems.
agent_relevance: Treat the Schön-to-LLM link as an analogy supported by self-correction literature, not by a direct test.
